_comment: Move 14 Phase E item E1 (U2): 'a rule applied in one place, not mirrored to its twin' has now
hit three confirmed instances (REG-89, REG-104, REG-112) -- the same threshold that earned X0 a
permanent registry+gate. This is that gate for the twin-pair-divergence family. Each rule below
names two or more locations that must move together; check-twin-pair-consistency.py fails when
they diverge. A human adds a new rule here when a new twin-pair is found (mirroring how
scripts/quality/x0-evaluator-registry.json is curated) -- this file does not invent new pairs on

rules.description: Test classes sharing the same vulnerable pattern (a single-arg constructor that silently prefers an external generated-app path over its classpath-baked fixture, per REG-103) must be excluded from a generated app's own `test` task TOGETHER -- excluding only one sibling and not the other is exactly REG-112's shape.

A top-level model array field contributed by a pack/fragment (not just the app's own root) must be threaded through ModelSourceResolver.MODEL_ARRAY_KEYS, BOTH copies of pack.schema.json, ModelResolver.resolve(), and the CompiledModelCanonicalJson/Reader pair -- CLAUDE.md's own documented four-place rule. PACK-11 (2026-08-17) extended this to aggregates/autoPanels/documents/guidePages (`selectors` has its own rule -- it is expanded, not serialized), found by machine-diffing the composer's key set against the real top-level schema keys: four were missing from BOTH the composer and pack.schema.json, and guidePages was the asymmetric case -- merged by the composer, rejected by the schema. Note the FIFTH place this rule does not cover: a member kind that carries references of its own also needs entries in ModelSourceResolver.rewriteKnownMemberReferenceFields, or it composes and then fails validation because its own `concept`/`query` stayed unqualified. That one fails loudly, which is why it is not tracked here.

A new AST-level field needs a live path through parser -> compiler -> canonical writer+reader -> ModelResolver, or it survives parsing but silently never reaches the generator/runtime (REG-104's shape: RolePermissions.toRole() had no diagnostic for an app-declared role because roles[] did not yet exist end to end).

rules.citedBy: B20 (S2, __OutsideRepo\s1\b20-design.md, ADR-0011); physicallyIsolate added S8 Wave 4 (ADR-0011 D4 v2)
rules.description: The contexts[] registry (which bounded contexts a model declares) needs the same live path the ast-compiled-four-place rule requires for roles[] -- parser, compiler, ModelResolver, and the canonical writer+reader pair -- or a declared context's registry entry survives parsing but silently never reaches the generator/runtime. physicallyIsolate (Wave 4, ADR-0011 D4's v2 opt-in) is a field ON each context entry, not a new top-level array, so it rides this same rule rather than a fourth one.

rules.citedBy: S7 Phase B (B13 declarative conversion vocabulary)
rules.description: conversions[] needs the same live path the ast-compiled-four-place rule requires for roles[] -- parser, compiler, ModelResolver, and the canonical writer+reader pair -- or a declared conversion survives parsing but silently never reaches the generator, which emits nothing under db/conversion-hooks/ and the author gets no error anywhere (the X0 shape REG-104 found for roles[]).

D3's import-gate field (imports[], declared on a context fragment, pack-shaped per D2) must stay schema-declared on BOTH pack.schema.json copies and enforced by ModelSourceResolver -- a copy that lost the schema key would reject every context fragment that declares imports[], and a resolver that lost the enforcement would silently let an undeclared cross-context reference through (the exact X0 shape D3 exists to prevent).

run-portable-tooling-check.ps1 asserts README.md contains these three EXACT command substrings verbatim (its own linuxCommandExamplesPresent check, case-sensitive .Contains()). F1/F3/F6's own doc edits to README.md all had to preserve them by hand with no gate telling them so beforehand -- this rule is that gate: an edit that reflows or rewords any of the three now fails loud instead of the check silently going red for a reason that looks unrelated to whatever the edit was actually about. md-zero-2026-08-11 PLAN.md Phase 5: README.md is now GENERATED from content/readme.yml (scripts/docs/generate_group_d_docs.py) -- pinned there instead, the actual place an editor now changes this text.

Same trap as readme-portable-tooling-substrings, for docs/GETTING_STARTED.md's two required substrings (run-portable-tooling-check.ps1's linuxCommandExamplesPresent check). F6's full rewrite of this file had to preserve both verbatim with no gate telling it so beforehand. md-zero-2026-08-11 PLAN.md Phase 5: docs/GETTING_STARTED.md is now GENERATED from content/getting-started.yml -- pinned there instead.

run-portable-tooling-check.ps1's cliReportBootstrapCallable check separately asserts '.github/workflows/npdev-ci-validation.yml' contains the exact substring './npdev report bootstrap' -- a third location for the same literal string this script depends on, found while registering the README/GETTING_STARTED trap above (not itself part of §0's stated five, but the identical failure shape).

scripts/quality/schema-consumers.json's own PROTECTED entry for generate_dsl_reference.py names check-dsl-reference-output-floor.py as its enforcing gate -- if a future refactor renames or removes that script from run-generator-gate.ps1 without updating the registry (or vice versa), the registry silently claims protection that no longer runs, exactly the 'consumers nobody enumerated' shape this whole item exists to close. Both must name the enforcing script consistently.

ledger/boundaries/B16.yml declares codeLinked:true, naming ValidationDiagnosticNormalizer.java's DESCOPED_PROPERTY_BOUNDARY_IDS map as B16's real enforcement. If a future refactor removes the 'B16' mapping from that Java file without updating the registry entry (or vice versa -- someone adds a new boundaryId string in code without a matching ledger/boundaries/*.yml file), the registry would claim a code link that does not exist, or code would silently attach an unregistered boundaryId -- the exact 'every hittable boundary has an enforcing code, and vice versa' check REG-135 names as its own twin-pair gate.

Eleven independent copies of NPDev's external-build-root resolution must agree on HOW they find the repo root, because Gradle writes build output to the root they compute and the PowerShell/Python tooling reads it back from the root THEY compute. They used to walk up looking for a directory literally NAMED 'NPDev_General'; a clone named anything else (GitHub checks this repo out as 'NPDevGeneral') made every copy fall through to its own fallback, and the fallbacks disagreed -- measured in a real renamed clone: NPDevKernel resolved to <clone>/Build, NPDevContract/dsl to <clone>/NPDevContract/Build, and Get-NPDevBuildRoot to <clone>/../Build. THREE roots. Gradle built 30 adapter jars into one and sync-runtimehost-libs.ps1 searched another, so three packaged-app proof tests failed on Linux CI for twelve days while passing locally, because the author's directory really is named NPDev_General and the walk succeeded there by coincidence. All eleven now identify the repo root by its CONTENTS (the NPDevContract + NPDevGenerator + NPDevKernel modules), never by its name, and each carries the 'npdev-build-root-resolution' token so dropping one is a gate failure rather than a silent return to three roots. BT-1 added a twelfth copy (NPDevRuntimeHost/runtimehost-core/build.gradle) for the same reason -- the id keeps its original 'eleven' name (an identifier, not a live count) rather than risk a rename breaking something that refers to it by string.

runtimehost-core/build.gradle's Spring Boot BOM version must match NPDevRuntimeHost/build.gradle.template's `org.springframework.boot` plugin version -- NOT NPDevRuntimeHost/build.gradle's own stale pin, kept only for running the RuntimeHost gate directly against a bare template checkout. build.gradle.template is the file every generated app actually gets; a generated app links the app-coupled bridge (compiled against whatever build.gradle.template pins) against the runtimehost-core.jar dependency (compiled against whatever this rule's other file pins) on the SAME runtime classpath, so the two must agree or the jar and the app's own compiled bridge code can silently diverge at runtime -- exactly the divergence build.gradle.template's own R1c comment already measured live for bootJar/mockito/archunit under Gradle 9 when NPDevRuntimeHost/build.gradle was still out of step.

THREE independent places turn a model name into SQL identifier text, and all three must ask SqlDialect.identifier() -- the conditional quoting that lets a field be named `order`. SchemaRealizationEmitter EMITS the DDL; JdbcBusinessConceptStore READS AND WRITES rows against it; SchemaLifecycleExecutor.quotedIdentifier serves the 40 schema-lifecycle sites (impact probe, backfill, rename, widen, unique) that only run when something CHANGES on an existing database. Quoting one alone is worse than quoting none: the app builds, boots, and cannot find its own table. The third seam was NOT in STOR-6's plan -- the plan named two, and the third surfaced only when a live H2 run hit `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM probe_reserveds WHERE order IS NOT NULL` during an impact probe, which no fresh-database test can ever reach. Each carries the 'npdev-sql-identifier-quoting' token so dropping one is a gate failure. Cover is NPDevSamples/probes/engine-probe, whose ProbeRecord has columns `order` and `value` and whose Row concept realizes to the table `rows`; run-engine-app-proof.py asserts they round-trip on every engine.

THREE places have to agree on where a generated app keeps its database, and they are reached by different callers so no one of them can catch a drift in the others. UserDatabaseDefinitionLoader DECIDES the app-relative root (and composes it into spring.datasource.url, which Spring resolves at boot); OperationalRunbookEmitter RESOLVES it back to an absolute path for the five _ops scripts, one of which does `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` on it; FinalAppAssembler SPARES it when deleteBeforeMount wipes the FinalApp tree on regeneration. Disagreement between the first two is QUAL-3 again -- one database with two front doors, where resetting via one destroys data the other is serving. Disagreement with the third is silent data loss on the next regeneration, which would ALSO leave every schema-evolution test green against a fresh database instead of the existing one it exists to exercise. Each carries the 'npdev-app-data-root-anchor' token so dropping one fails run-ai-knowledge-gate.ps1. Cover is AppIdentityIsolationTest plus the copy-the-app-elsewhere-and-boot proof recorded on PORT-1.

allowSideBySide (a direct pack import tolerating a different-file collision with the same real packId resolved elsewhere in the transitive graph) is declared on model.schema.json's packRef $defs entry in all 4 mirrored copies, AND must stay recognized by ModelSourceResolver.validateNoMalformedRef's per-path extra-keys allowlist (a structural guard that runs BEFORE resolution and would otherwise reject the key as malformed before PackDependencyGraphWalker's own enforcement ever ran -- this exact gap shipped once in PK-3's own first draft, caught only by its own test suite), AND must stay enforced in PackDependencyGraphWalker.java, which is where the check/refusal/warning actually live. Losing any one of these leaves the schema accepting a key nothing enforces, or a key nothing can even author past the earlier structural gate.

satelliteOf (a concept-level marker declaring a 1:1 satellite relationship to a base concept owned by another pack, PACK-ROADMAP.md card PK-6) needs the same live path the ast-compiled-four-place rule requires for roles[] -- parser, compiler, ModelResolver (BOTH of its ConceptAst-reconstructing sites, sanitizeConcept and mergeConcept -- a concept-level field is easy to drop at exactly this point, unlike a top-level array field), and the canonical writer+reader pair -- or a declared satellite marker survives parsing but silently never reaches SemanticValidator/the generator (REG-104's exact shape). Deliberately named 'satelliteOf', not 'extends': ConceptAst/model.schema.json's concept.extends already means single-model concept inheritance (field merging via ModelResolver.mergeConcept) -- reusing that keyword for a completely different cross-pack FK-bond marker would have collided with existing, load-bearing semantics.

origin (pack-attribution provenance -- packId/packVersion/packDigest/sealed -- attached to every Compiled*/*Ast member type PACK-2 covers: concept, query, event, flow, capability, role, panel, domain type) needs the same live path the ast-compiled-four-place rule requires for roles[] -- parser, compiler, ModelResolver (every ConceptAst/CapabilityAst/EventAst/FlowAst-reconstructing site: sanitizeX and mergeX both, same 'a per-member field is easy to drop at exactly this point' reasoning satelliteOf's own entry gives), and the canonical writer+reader pair -- or a member's pack attribution survives parsing but silently never reaches the generator/runtime (REG-104's exact shape). ModelSourceResolver.recordOrigin (where a pack-contributed member's origin is actually computed and recorded, keyed by MODEL_ARRAY_KEYS kind + qualified name) is deliberately NOT one of these four -- unlike an authored field, origin is resolver-DERIVED data with no pack.schema.json/model.schema.json surface, so it does not ride the separate pack-composition-four-place rule either; its own chain (ResolutionState -> ResolvedModelSource -> JsonModelParser's originByQualifiedMemberName lookup) is covered by NPDevContract/dsl's existing pack-composition test suite (737 tests green at PACK-2's own close), not this registry rule.

The list of <FinalApp>/App directories that regeneration must NOT delete is decided independently in three places that all run during one build -- Build-NpdevApp.ps1's $SparedInsideApp, Build-ClaudeApp.ps1's copy of it, and FinalAppAssembler.PRESERVED_APP_DIRECTORIES. The Java layer runs LAST, so a directory added to a PowerShell list and not to the Java one is spared and then deleted again, silently, in the same build: exactly what happened to `logs` between MONITOR_PLAN D10 and the agent-proxy work. Anything holding state the generator cannot reproduce -- the database, the log archive, the operator-written secrets/agent-proxy.env -- must appear in all three.

The FOURTH runtime-supported-controller enforcement point, distinct from the three runtime-supported-controllers.json enforcement points (RuntimeControllerAllowlistConfig, build.gradle.template's unsupportedRuntimeHostControllerSources, run-runtime-surface-evidence.ps1) that all key off com/finalexec/api plus one fixed, per-app-identical manifest. A plugin controller is author-supplied and lives under the reserved com.npdev.generated.plugin. package instead, with a PER-APP security posture generated from the model's own capability.plugin.json descriptors -- so it needs its own mechanism, not a fourth use of the existing three (adding its name to allowedControllers would neither enable it, wrong package, nor be architecturally sound, since that manifest must not vary per app). GeneratedPluginMountPlan validates the descriptor (controllerClass package prefix, mount.basePath prefix, security.minimumRole required) at generation time and refuses to generate an unguarded mount; RuntimeApiEmitter copies the controller source and writes the per-app npdev/plugin-controllers/plugin-controller-security.json manifest; NPDevRuntimeHost's PluginControllerSecurityConfig reads that manifest at boot, registers a role-checking HandlerInterceptor per mounted controller (D9: enforced by an emitted wrapper, not merely declared), and REFUSES TO START if any com.npdev.generated.plugin.*Controller bean exists with no matching manifest entry. Losing any of the four leaves either a controller descriptor nothing enforces at request time, or a security manifest nothing emits/reads, or a guard that can never fire because the mount it should be watching was never wired to it -- the exact 'three enforcement points, one forgotten' shape this rule exists to catch before a fifth session repeats it. The proof script is included because D9's own security.minimumRole enforcement (a live 403 against an under-privileged caller) is verified there, not in a JUnit test: PluginControllerSecurityConfig imports com.npdev.generated.*, so build.gradle.template's generatedRuntimeDependentMainSources exclusion means it compiles ONLY inside an assembled app and never in a bare-template unit test (CLAUDE.md: 'RuntimeHost tests that name com.npdev.generated. never run in any gate').

CapabilityExecutionPolicy (kernel) and CompiledCapabilityExecutionPolicy (DSL module) are independent classes with the same field-for-field shape (retryCount/retryDelayMs/timeoutMs/circuitOpenAfterFailures/circuitOpenMs/bulkheadMaxConcurrent/idempotencyKeyField/failureClassification) -- the kernel cannot depend on the DSL's compiled-model types, so there is no single shared type to enforce this instead. R8d (2026-08) deliberately left both untouched (adapter-level deadlines only, per the card's own sequencing: adapter deadlines first, the kernel-wide default -- CapabilityExecutionPolicy.defaults()'s zeros -- a separate, later decision). Registered here as groundwork for whoever DOES touch the kernel default or either shape next: a field added to one side without the other is exactly REG-104's 'parses/compiles clean, never reaches the runtime on the skipped side' shape. Each class carries the 'npdev-capability-execution-policy-mirror' token in its javadoc so dropping one (e.g. a rewrite that deletes the class) is a gate failure rather than a silent divergence.

The pack/context member-qualification rule (a context qualifies by its declared `contexts[]` name; a pack by its `as` alias if the import declares one, else by the pack file's own `pack` id; members merge as `qualifier::name`) now exists in TWO languages. Java's ModelSourceResolver is authoritative -- the generator only ever reads the Java-resolved model. REG-186 added a narrow Python copy so the build-free introspection commands can see pack/context members without a Gradle run. Both carry the `npdev-qualifier-rule` token; dropping it from either is the REG-108 'two walks of the same graph that drift' shape and fails this gate.

`selectors` is threaded like every other pack-contributable array EXCEPT at the last step: it never reaches the canonical compiled JSON, because ModelCompiler expands each selector into a picker panel and the PANEL is what round-trips. So its fourth place is the expansion loop in ModelCompiler, not CompiledModelCanonicalJson. Tracked separately rather than exempted from pack-composition-four-place: an exemption would leave the key looking guarded while nothing checked it, and this way deleting the expansion breaks the gate instead of silently producing a model whose selectors vanish.
